title: Deep Composition Delegations (Simulated Inheritance)
pattern: A nested struct layout where parent structs implement manual, boilerplate delegation methods for almost every single method defined on their inner fields, trying to mimic physical class inheritance.
why_bad: Bloats the codebase with dummy forwarding methods that add zero business value. It creates highly fragile structures; any method added or modified on the inner child forces a cascading change in all parent delegation chains.
detection: Look for structs containing methods that do nothing except forward calls to an inner field with an identical name and signature.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. The Facade pattern, where a public entry point delegates to highly complex internal subsystems to provide a simplified API.
fix: Expose the inner component directly if it has no invariants to protect, or rethink the design to avoid deep physical containment.
source: *Martin Fowler - Refactoring (1999)*, Chapter 3, "Message Chains" / "Middle Man"; *Steve McConnell - Code Complete (2004)*, Chapter 6.
